key_findings.finding: The transformation is desilylation of a silyl ether to the corresponding terminal alcohol. The likely protecting group is tert-butyldimethylsilyl (TBDMS/TBS), characterized by Si bonded to O, two methyl groups, and a tert-butyl group; the reaction record directly shows conversion of a TBS-protected alcohol to OH under chloride/acidic workup conditions.

source_tools.relevance: Direct reaction record showing O–Si(CH3)2–tert-butyl cleavage to the alcohol

key_findings.finding: For a complex substrate bearing esters, an alkyne, heteroaromatic nitrogens, and a cyclic ether, the usual first-choice conditions are fluoride-mediated cleavage such as TBAF in dry THF at 0 °C to room temperature, often with controlled or buffered fluoride. Alternative commonly used conditions are NH4F in methanol/alcohol solvent or HF·pyridine/Et3N·3HF when stronger silyl-ether cleavage is needed; ester and alkyne compatibility is generally best assessed with mild, near-neutral fluoride conditions and short reaction times.
